narrative: Revenue looks healthy but the account is quietly trading down: three mid-to-high value categories collapsed while cheaper Consumables and Cleaning lines filled the gap. Margin fell from 25.6% to 17.3% and high-tier share dropped 27 points even as topline revenue stayed flat. This is structural — the declines are 9-10 months old, unrecovered, and match no seasonal pattern.
cited_evidence: Margin fell from 25.6% to 17.3%, down 8.3 points, starting around October 2025 while revenue held flat.
High-tier product share collapsed from 40.4% to 13.4%, a 27-point drop, the sharpest shift measured on this account.
Power Tools revenue fell from a median ₹47,955 to ₹10,548 a month after October 2025, a 78% decline unrecovered after 10 months.
Diagnostic Equipment dropped from ₹33,297 to ₹3,959 a month after December 2025, an 88% decline sustained for 9 months.
Precision Hardware fell from ₹26,167 to ₹4,074 a month over the same period, an 84% decline with no recovery.
recommended_actions: Contact the account to understand why Power Tools and Diagnostic Equipment orders stopped.
Check whether a competitor is now supplying these three categories.
Push for reinstated high-tier and diagnostic purchasing before renewing the account plan.

margin_impact.basis: Current monthly revenue valued at the baseline margin rate, minus the margin actually earned. Isolates the rate change from any change in volume.

prioritization.reason: 43.1% of baseline monthly revenue at risk; 33.5% of baseline monthly gross margin at risk, high confidence.

churn_risk_projection.basis: Assumes the current monthly loss rate persists unchanged for 12 months — not a forecast of further deterioration, just the cost of inaction at today's rate. Revenue and margin figures overlap and must not be added together.

model_opinion.drivers_note: No single fact carries this read: hiding any one of them moves the leading probability by under 5 points, because several point the same way.

model_agreement.agent_response: Agree: sustained, significant margin erosion and tier downgrade across three categories confirm genuine leakage, not noise.

evidence_timeline.headline: History begins
evidence_timeline.detail: 23.3 months of history, 31 orders across 8 categories. Data sufficiency: sufficient (score 1.0).

evidence_timeline.headline: Power Tools revenue steps down 78.0%
evidence_timeline.detail: Monthly revenue Rs 47,955 -> Rs 10,548 (78.0%); 17.9% of this account's baseline revenue. Sustained 10 months. No prior-year echo, so seasonality does not explain it.
evidence_timeline.method: The stricter multi-year seasonal check needs about three years of history and could not run; the prior-year echo above is the check 24 months can support.

evidence_timeline.headline: Margin rate erodes
evidence_timeline.detail: Margin rate 25.6% -> 17.3% (-8.3pp). 10 months sat below the normal range. It first fell below in 2025-11 and has stayed there since.
evidence_timeline.method: Erosion threshold: 3.0pp between the baseline and recent windows.

evidence_timeline.headline: Product mix downgrades
evidence_timeline.detail: High-tier share of revenue 40.4% -> 13.4% (-27.0pp). Low tier 37.1% -> 68.3%. Value is moving out of the high tier and being backfilled by cheaper lines. High-tier share first fell below its normal range in 2025-11 and has stayed there since.
evidence_timeline.method: Shift threshold: 8.0pp. Direction decides the verdict — the same size of move upward is premiumisation, not a downgrade.

evidence_timeline.headline: Diagnostic Equipment revenue steps down 88.1%
evidence_timeline.detail: Monthly revenue Rs 33,297 -> Rs 3,959 (88.1%); 12.4% of this account's baseline revenue. Sustained 9 months. No prior-year echo, so seasonality does not explain it.
evidence_timeline.method: The stricter multi-year seasonal check needs about three years of history and could not run; the prior-year echo above is the check 24 months can support.

evidence_timeline.headline: Precision Hardware revenue steps down 84.4%
evidence_timeline.detail: Monthly revenue Rs 26,167 -> Rs 4,074 (84.4%); 10.0% of this account's baseline revenue. Sustained 9 months. No prior-year echo, so seasonality does not explain it.
evidence_timeline.method: The stricter multi-year seasonal check needs about three years of history and could not run; the prior-year echo above is the check 24 months can support.

evidence_timeline.headline: Revenue is stable
evidence_timeline.detail: First half vs second half 0.4%, trend 0.14%/month. A stable topline does not by itself mean a healthy account — the margin, discount and mix rows are what test that.
evidence_timeline.method: Material decline requires both <= -15.0% half-over-half and <= -1.50%/month trend.

evidence_timeline.headline: Discounting is stable
evidence_timeline.method: Creep threshold: 3.0pp. Discount is revenue-weighted, so a deep discount on a large line counts for more than the same discount on a small one.

evidence_timeline.headline: Ordering behaviour is unchanged
evidence_timeline.detail: Orders per month 1.28 -> 1.33 (3.9%); lines per order 6.65 -> 5.62 (-15.5%); average order value -1.1%.

evidence_timeline.headline: Seasonality checked: no recent dip to explain
evidence_timeline.detail: No month in the last year fell far enough below normal to need explaining.

material_thresholds.note: material if (halves AND slope) are met, OR the recent-vs-baseline drop is

breakdown.note: Lines share the account's expected months of continued buying, so their values add back to the account total. Line losses can exceed the account's value at risk because lines that grew offset part of the loss.

_lifetime_value.note: Lifetime value = value per month x the horizon months (12 or 24), flat. Expected orders and expected active months (BG/NBD, fitted on the whole book) are reported alongside for information and do not scale the money. Baseline uses the value per month before the recent window; current uses the recent window. Value at risk is the gap — the same loss the monthly figures show, on a longer clock. Never add it to monthly revenue at risk.
